chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Among the most blissful of My friends in My Presence is a believing servant who has a share of righteousness, who worships his Lord well, and worships Allah in secret. He was hidden among the people so that he was not pointed at by fingers, and his sustenance was sufficient (at subsistence level). So he was patient with it, and death hastened to him, so few were his inheritors and few were his mourners.'
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the most blissful believer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi from al-Kafi highlights the virtue of 'ghub' (hiddenness), where a believer’s sincere worship and patience with modest sustenance (kafaaf) earn divine pleasure despite a lack of worldly fame. The mention of early death and few mourners underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual merit of the common believer over the prominent, reflecting the concept of 'tawassul' through humble piety rather than public recognition. This narrative aligns with the broader Shia tradition of valuing inner purity and endurance of hardship as signs of true closeness to Allah.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Bakr Bin Muhammad Al Azdy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “The most blissful of My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> friends in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Presence is a believing servant with a share from righteousness, good worship of his Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and he worships Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> in the secrecy, and he was hidden among the people, so he was not pointed at by the fingers, and his sustenance was at subsistence level. So he was patient upon it, and the death hastened to him, and few were his inheritors, and few were his mourners’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘The most enviable among My friends is a believer who has his share of salvation, performs the worship of his Lord well, worships Allah privately, is obscure among people and no finger rises to point him out. His sustenance is only adequate for his basic needs and he bears it patiently. I cause him to die faster, thus his legacy is little and his mourners are very few.’”
